title: Ramayana Opens North America Advance Bookings Early as Godzilla Minus Zero Looms
excerpt: Independent chains have published advance showtimes with a possible November 5 release; the film faces Takashi Yamazaki's Godzilla Minus Zero, tracking a $25 million North American opening.
body:
• Advance bookings for Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part One have begun in North America, with independent cinema chains publishing advance showtimes ahead of the Diwali release.
  • AMC locations and California cinemas are yet to appear in listings, and no IMAX shows have been listed yet — the film was made specifically for premium large-format screens.
  • Reports suggest the India release could move up to November 5, with paid previews on November 4 in several countries including North America; Sony has updated the North American date to November 5.
  • The film faces Godzilla Minus Zero, releasing November 6 in North America, which is tracking a $25 million opening weekend and carries a 97% Rotten Tomatoes score.

Bookings open, IMAX awaited

Ramayana: Part One is on sale. Advance bookings have begun in North America ahead of the film's Diwali-season release, with independent cinema chains publishing advance showtimes. AMC locations and California cinemas are yet to appear in the listings, and no IMAX shows have been listed yet — the screenings that matter most for a film built specifically for the big screen. Advance ticket sales are expected to pick up sharply once IMAX slots open.

"The film faces Godzilla Minus Zero, releasing November 6 in North America, which is tracking a $25 million opening weekend and carries a 97% Rotten Tomatoes score."

https://x.com/Cinemaaforu/status/2108758389266460796

The release date itself is in flux. Reports indicate the India release could advance to November 5, ditching the original Diwali date of November 8, with paid previews planned for the evening of November 4 in several countries including North America. Sony Pictures has updated the North American release date to November 5 from November 6. In the UK, South Africa, and Mauritius, the film is currently scheduled for November 6.

The film

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Part One stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana, with Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshmana. It is the first of a two-part epic, with the second installment slated for Diwali 2027 — among the most ambitious and expensive productions in Indian cinema history, and notably releasing on November 6, which is Ranbir Kapoor's daughter Raha's birthday.

The Godzilla in the room

Sharing the frame is Godzilla Minus Zero, Takashi Yamazaki's sequel to Godzilla Minus One, arriving in North American theatres on November 6 with a special Godzilla Day IMAX early-access screening on November 3. Early tracking suggests a $25 million opening weekend — more than double the $11.4 million that Minus One earned in 2023 — and the film carries a 97% Rotten Tomatoes score from 32 critics, with growing Best Picture Oscar buzz. It is also billed as the first Japanese production filmed for IMAX.

The two films will compete directly for premium-format screens. In India, according to trade reports, Godzilla Minus Zero will get limited IMAX showcasing — likely just one show at most IMAX properties, with the rest allotted to Ramayana, which is expected to command far greater demand.

What it means for the diaspora

For Indian audiences in the US and Canada, this is the biggest desi theatrical event of the year: a mythological epic engineered for IMAX, timed to Diwali. Book early once IMAX shows list — premium-format screens for Indian films in North America sell out fast, and the November 5 advance means opening-weekend demand will concentrate. The Ramayana-versus-Godzilla faceoff is also a rare box-office experiment: gods versus monsters, opening a day apart, in the same theatres.

What to watch

Whether the November 5 advance is formally locked (makers are expected to confirm within days), when IMAX bookings open in North America, and whether the paid-preview strategy on November 4 sets opening-day records for an Indian film in the diaspora market.
